# Physiology, Fascia

**Authors:** Tom George, Orlando De Jesus

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Several interpretations of the term "fascia" exist within the research community, with no singular agreed-upon definition. However, in simplest terms, fascia can be described as a thin layer of connective tissue that separates muscles and organs from other structures within the body. It supports and protects muscles and internal organs and reduces friction between muscles. Fascia also forms distinct muscular compartments, provides attachments, and improves circulation.
